items.name: Zeolite Catalyst
items.lore: A crystal full of molecule-sized pores; reactions that fit inside go faster.

items.name: Molecular Orbital Lattice
items.lore: Electron wavefunctions shared between atoms, frozen into a grid. This is what a chemical bond is.

items.name: Chiral Crystal
items.lore: Left-handed or right-handed, never both. Life only uses one hand.

items.name: Electride Crystal
items.lore: A salt whose negative ions are bare electrons sitting in holes in the lattice.

items.name: Graphene Sheet
items.lore: Carbon one atom thick. Stronger than steel, conducts better than copper.

items.name: Carbon Nanotube Bundle
items.lore: Graphene rolled into tubes, the tubes twisted into rope.

items.name: Buckyball Cage
items.lore: Sixty carbon atoms arranged like a football - with room inside for one more atom.

items.name: Metal-Organic Framework
items.lore: Metal nodes, organic struts: a sponge with more inner surface than a football pitch per gram.

items.name: Noble Gas Clathrate
items.lore: Xenon caged in ice. The noble gases are not as aloof as the textbooks said.

items.name: Self-Healing Polymer
items.lore: Cut it and the chains find each other again.

items.name: Room-Temperature Superconductor
items.lore: Zero resistance without cryogenics. Physicists have chased this for a century.

items.name: Positronium Hydride
items.lore: A molecule made of a hydrogen atom and an atom of matter bound to antimatter. It lasts a nanosecond - unless you trap it.

items.name: Muonic Catalyst
items.lore: Swap an electron for a muon and atoms shrink 200 times - close enough to fuse cold.

items.name: Flerovium Ingot
items.lore: Element 114, held together by magic numbers of protons and neutrons.

items.name: Unbihexium Ingot
items.lore: Element 126, the heart of the island of stability. Nothing should be this heavy and last this long.

items.name: Gene Sampler
items.lore: Use on any creature to take a genome sample. Creatures from other dimensions give xenogenome samples.

items.name: Genome Sample
items.lore: Every instruction for building one creature, in a vial.

items.name: Xenogenome Sample
items.lore: A genome from a creature of another dimension. Its code is not written in DNA.

items.name: Recombinant DNA
items.lore: A double helix spliced from more than one creature.

items.name: Engineered Enzyme
items.lore: A protein designed to speed up exactly one reaction a millionfold.

items.name: Folded Protein Crystal
items.lore: A chain of amino acids that found its one shape out of more than the universe has atoms.

items.name: Stem Cell Culture
items.lore: Cells that have not yet decided what to become.

items.name: Minimal Synthetic Cell
items.lore: The smallest genome that can still be alive, written from scratch.

items.name: Xenobot Swarm
items.lore: Living machines made of cells, designed by an evolutionary algorithm.

items.name: Tardigrade Culture
items.lore: Survives vacuum, radiation and freezing by simply pausing being alive.

items.name: Quantum Chlorophyll
items.lore: Photosynthesis moves energy by trying every path at once - coherently.

items.name: Cryptochrome Magnetoreceptor
items.lore: The protein in a robin's eye that feels Earth's field through entangled radical pairs.

items.name: Neural Organoid
items.lore: A pea-sized brain grown in a dish. It has started to dream.

items.name: Turing Morphogen
items.lore: Two chemicals, one fast and one slow, that paint stripes and spots by themselves.

items.name: Silicon Life Spore
items.lore: Life built on silicon instead of carbon. It grew in the Bulk.

items.name: Telomerase Complex
items.lore: Rebuilds the clocks at the ends of chromosomes. Cells that have it do not age.

items.name: Spark of Life
items.lore: The moment chemistry became biology, caught and kept.

items.name: Panspermia Seed
items.lore: Life packed to survive the trip between universes.

items.name: Omnicellular Genome
items.lore: One genome that can build any creature in any dimension.

items.name: Empty Containment Cell
items.lore: A magnetically sealed flask for fluids too hot, too cold or too strange for a bucket. Scoop a source block or fill it from a tank.

items.name: Assembly Matrix
items.lore: A femtoscale jig that holds a hundred parts in exactly the right place while the Extreme Assembly Table joins them.

items.name: Hyperlattice Frame
items.lore: A scaffold folded through a fourth dimension, so a nine-by-nine assembly has room for its insides.

items.name: Transfinite Weave
items.lore: Cloth with more threads than there are numbers to count them. Endgame assemblies are stitched on it.

items.name: Oracle's Lemma
items.lore: Creative mode only. Use inside one of Alpha Omega's trial chambers to have it count as solved.

items.name: CPT Mirror
items.lore: Reverses charge, parity and time at once. Through it lies a universe exactly like ours, made of antimatter.

items.name: Penning Harness
items.lore: A wearable Penning trap: magnetic and electric fields that keep every atom of you from touching the Antiverse.

items.name: Antiproton Bundle
items.lore: A few billion antiprotons, slowed from near light speed and held in a magnetic bottle.

items.name: Raw Anti-Iron
items.lore: Ore from the Antiverse. Iron, exactly - except that every particle in it is the opposite one.

items.name: Anti-Iron Ingot
items.lore: Anti-iron, refined in levitation. Its surface never touches the mould.

items.name: Raw Anti-Gold
items.lore: Gold of the mirror universe, cold blue where ours is warm yellow - only the light it reflects is the same.

items.name: Anti-Gold Ingot
items.lore: Anti-gold: as soft, as dense and as noble as gold. Do not wear it.

items.name: Anticarbon Crystal
items.lore: Antidiamond. Four antibonds per anti-atom, as hard as diamond.

items.name: Antisilicon Shard
items.lore: Semiconductor of the Antiverse - its holes are positrons.

items.name: Antihydrogen Crystal
items.lore: Frozen antihydrogen: one antiproton, one positron, a few kelvin.

items.name: Antihelium Nucleus
items.lore: Two antiprotons and two antineutrons. Our own detectors have glimpsed a handful; the Antiverse is full of them.

items.name: Antiquark Shard
items.lore: Confined anti-colour charge, chipped from a creature of the Antiverse.

items.name: Mirror Alloy Ingot
items.lore: Matter and antimatter in alternating grains, a Penning field between every pair. It hums.

items.name: Mirror Processor
items.lore: Antisilicon logic on an anticarbon die: it computes with positrons.

items.name: Baryogenesis Seed
items.lore: Out of equilibrium, violating baryon number, C and CP: the three conditions for a universe to end up made of something.

items.name: Shard of Omnipotence
items.lore: A splinter of the Core that made anything. It still remembers how - it has only forgotten what.

items.name: Echo of the Transcendental
items.lore: The last ringing of a destroyed dimension, caught before it faded. It is the shape of the place, without the place.

items.name: Omnipotence Dust
items.lore: Ground Omnipotence. Each grain can still be anything - for a moment.

items.name: Apeiron Ingot
items.lore: Anaximander's apeiron: the boundless stuff everything else is cut from. The ingot has edges only where you look.

items.name: Pleroma Crystal
items.lore: Pleroma - the fullness. Every law the Transcendental held, frozen into one lattice.

items.name: Logos Thread
items.lore: A strand of the Word that orders the world. Wound into a coil it makes space obey a shape.

items.name: Rekindled Spark
items.lore: What the Pleroma Reconstitutor leaves behind once the Transcendental is whole again: the first light of the second creation.

items.name: Omnipotent Ingot
items.lore: Metal that is whatever metal it needs to be. Forged at the reborn Core, out of the boundless and the dust of the old Core.

items.name: Crystal of Transcendence
items.lore: A crystal that has stepped outside every system that could describe it.

items.name: Absolute Singularity
items.lore: Not a point where the laws break down: a point where there are no laws to break.

items.name: Eschaton Core
items.lore: The end of all things, held still in a cage of Omnipotent metal. Every endgame artefact is built around one.

items.name: Omnipotent Edge
items.lore: A blade with no thickness and no limit. What it cuts has never existed.

items.name: Scepter of Singularities
items.lore: It does not fire singularities. It decides where one has always been.

items.name: Crown of Transcendence
items.lore: You see everything, because nothing can hide from what is outside it.

items.name: Mantle of Omnipotence
items.lore: Harm needs a law to happen by. You are wearing all of them.

items.name: Greaves of the Absolute
items.lore: Distance is a law. You may keep it or not.

items.name: Treads of Infinity
items.lore: Every step lands. None of them fall.

items.name: Lawgiver's Codex
items.lore: Blank, until you write. Then the place you stand in obeys what you wrote.

items.name: Coherent Wiring Harness
items.lore: Superconducting wire braided so its electrons keep their phase from end to end. Every quantum machine is threaded with it.

items.name: Entangled Bus Bar
items.lore: Two bars that are one: a current at one end is already at the other.

items.name: Chronoplastic Gasket
items.lore: Seals a joint against time itself: what is inside ages at the machine's pace, not the world's.

items.name: Spacetime Bearing
items.lore: Turns on a frictionless geodesic. It will outlast the machine around it.

items.name: Cosmic Flux Coupler
items.lore: Couples a machine to the flux of a whole cosmos without being consumed by it.

items.name: Ontological Junction
items.lore: Where a machine's idea of itself meets its matter. Without one, big machines forget what they are for.

items.name: Transfinite Lattice Bolt
items.lore: Threaded with ℵ₀ turns. It never quite finishes screwing in, and it never comes loose.

items.name: Omnilex Seal
items.lore: A wax seal pressed with a law. Machines that bear one are permitted to work.

items.name: Laplace's Demon
items.lore: An intellect that knows every force and every position. Shown a machine, it knows exactly how the machine must be run.

items.name: Morphogenic Serum
items.lore: Every signal an embryo listens to, in one vial. A Breached Anomaly Engine spends one on every creature it grows.

items.name: Akashic Record
items.lore: Everything that has ever been known, written once. Creative mode only.

items.name: Censer of Entropy
items.lore: Swing it and the world remembers how to decay. Any affliction, on one creature or on a place.

items.name: Singularity
items.lore: A singularity of something from another mod (or added by your pack).

items.name: Singularity Cluster
items.lore: Nine singularities condensed into one, when there are too many to hold.

items.name: Simulated Universe
items.lore: A whole other world, run from its first instant to its last inside the Forge. Each mod has its own.

items.name: Specimen Bundle
items.lore: One of everything a mod's world grows or leaves behind, sealed in glass.

items.name: Phase-Locked Stabiliser
items.lore: Locks a multiblock's fields to a reference oscillator. Drift comes slower and smaller.

items.name: Adaptive Feedback Core
items.lore: Learns how its machine wanders and leans against it before it does.

items.name: Predictive Lattice Governor
items.lore: Simulates the machine a minute ahead and corrects what has not happened yet.

items.name: Equilibrium Lattice
items.lore: Forged with Omnipotence: a law that says this machine does not change. It does not.

items.name: Rekindled Heart
items.lore: Four sparks of the second creation, beating together around an Eschaton Core.

items.name: Echo Lattice
items.lore: Echoes of the Transcendental, crossed and woven into a frame that remembers the shape of a world.

items.name: Seed of Omnipotence
items.lore: Everything a Core needs to grow, folded small: a heart, a remembered world, and the proof that it can be done.

items.name: Hand of the Demiurge
items.lore: The craftsman of the world had to hold it somehow. The only thing that can tune, wake or move an Omnipotence Core.

items.name: Dodecaract Excavator
items.lore: A cube with twelve dimensions has 4096 corners. One of them is always already inside the rock.

items.name: Eschaton Cell
items.lore: The end of all things, metered out in doses. What the last artefacts burn to stay what they are.

items.name: Primordial Nucleosynthesis Ash
items.lore: What the first three minutes made: three parts hydrogen to one of helium-4, a pinch of deuterium and helium-3, a trace of lithium-7.

items.name: Inflaton Condensate
items.lore: A scalar field held at the top of its potential, rolling so slowly that space doubles many times before it moves.

items.name: Baryon Asymmetry Crystal
items.lore: One extra quark in every billion pairs. Everything that was not annihilated grew out of that one part in a billion.

items.name: Metastable Vacuum Lattice
items.lore: The Higgs potential mapped out to the Planck scale: the valley we live in is not the deepest one. Held in a lattice of Higgs field capacitors.

items.name: No-Boundary Seed
items.lore: A closed universe tunnelled from nothing: round, without an edge, and without a first moment of time.

items.name: Aeon Boundary Shard
items.lore: Rescale an infinitely old, empty, massless universe and it looks like a Big Bang. A sliver of the seam between two aeons.

items.name: Proton Decay Residue
items.lore: Positrons and neutral pions from protons that lived 10^34 years and then simply came apart.

items.name: Last Flash of a Black Hole
items.lore: The final second of an evaporating black hole: hotter and brighter the smaller it gets, until nothing is left but the light.

items.name: Phantom Energy Cell
items.lore: Dark energy with w below -1. Its density grows as space expands, until it tears apart galaxies, stars, atoms - and then the cell.

items.name: Bounce Core
items.lore: A universe crushed to the Planck density, where the quantum geometry of space turned the collapse around.

items.name: True Vacuum Seed
items.lore: A bubble of the deeper vacuum, held below its critical radius. Let it grow and it expands at the speed of light, forever.

items.name: Heat Death Ember
items.lore: The last warmth of a universe going cold: a little above the temperature of its own horizon, and falling.

items.name: De Sitter Horizon Shard
items.lore: A piece of the cosmic horizon of an empty, accelerating universe. It glows at 10^-30 K and holds 10^122 bits.

items.name: Boltzmann Fluctuation
items.lore: Wait long enough in a universe at equilibrium and anything happens by chance. This is the anything.

items.name: Contained Anomaly Specimen
items.lore: A sample of something that should not be, held in a quarantine field small enough to carry. It is still trying to get out.

items.name: Topological Defect Core
items.lore: A knot in a broken symmetry: the field could not agree which vacuum to fall into, so it kept both - and the seam between them cannot untie.

items.name: Prion Lattice
items.lore: Misfolded protein stacked into amyloid. Touch a healthy protein to it and the healthy one misfolds too: shape is the infection.

items.name: Anomalous Strain Culture
items.lore: Stem cells exposed to a contained anomaly. Their checkpoints are failing one by one: no p53, no brakes, no reason to stop dividing.

items.name: Undecidable Kernel
items.lore: A program no other program can predict: whether it halts is true or false, and provably unprovable. It runs on anyway.

items.name: Immortal Cell Line
items.lore: Telomerase switched back on: the chromosome ends rebuild themselves, and the cells forget how to grow old. They have outlived their donor.

items.name: Metastatic Spore
items.lore: A cluster of cells that has learned to leave: to slip its tissue, ride the blood and grow again somewhere it was never meant to be.

items.name: Quine Replicator
items.lore: A machine whose instructions contain a description of itself and an order to copy it. A von Neumann replicator, a virus, a meme.

items.name: Resistant Clone Colony
items.lore: The cells that survived the last treatment - and so the ones that make the next tumour. Selection, not malice.

items.name: Tumour Microenvironment Organoid
items.lore: An anomaly is never alone: here it has grown its own blood vessels, recruited its own stroma and taught the local immune cells to look away.

items.name: Contagion Network Map
items.lore: Every contact, every transmission, every node an infection passed through. Somewhere in it is the threshold where R crosses 1.

items.name: Local Law Violation
items.lore: A sliver of space where a conservation law quietly fails: charge appears from nothing, and the rest of physics has to make room.

items.name: Symbiont Culture
items.lore: The same anomaly, turned: it still copies itself, but now it pays its host back. Parasite and partner differ by one sign.

items.name: Anomaly Catalogue
items.lore: Every kind of anomaly you have contained, what it can do, how far it can spread and how big the largest one will be. Most are small; a few are not.

items.name: Quarantine Field Matrix
items.lore: A field that clears an anomaly faster than it can copy itself. It does not destroy anything - it only keeps R below one.

items.name: Apoptosis Trigger
items.lore: A CRISPR-written instruction that only an anomalous cell will read: a reminder of the death it was always supposed to accept.

items.name: CAR-T Cell Culture
items.lore: Killer T cells taught a new receptor: they hunt one marker, the anomaly's own, and they multiply as they find it.

items.name: Resolved Anomaly
items.lore: An anomaly explained: its strangeness measured, renormalised, and written back into the laws. It is just physics now. It always was.

items.name: Euclidean Anchor
items.lore: Euclid's fifth postulate, made to hold. Wherever its bearer stands, parallel lines stay parallel.

items.name: Telescope Mirror Blank
items.lore: A disc of glass ground to a paraboloid within a fraction of a wavelength, then silvered. Light from a whole star lands on one point.

items.name: Spectral Plate
items.lore: Starlight spread into a rainbow and caught on glass. The dark lines in it say which elements the light passed through.

items.name: Survey Map
items.lore: Heights, rivers and benchmarks, measured rather than guessed. Every line on it was walked.

items.name: Theodolite Lens
items.lore: A sighting lens on a graduated circle: two angles and one measured baseline, and every distance follows.

items.name: Geoid Model
items.lore: The true shape of the planet: not a sphere, not quite an ellipsoid, but the surface the sea would take if it could flow everywhere.

items.name: Sediment Core
items.lore: A tube of layered ground. Each band is a year, a flood or an ash fall, stacked in the order it happened.

items.name: Raw Pitchblende
items.lore: Uraninite: heavy, black and pitch-glossy. Marie and Pierre Curie found two new elements in it by following its radioactivity.

items.name: Radium Salt
items.lore: Ten milligrams of radium chloride, glowing faintly in the dark by its own decay. Handle it as little as you can.

items.name: Geiger Tube
items.lore: A thin wire in a tube of low-pressure gas at high voltage. One ionising particle and the whole tube avalanches into a click.

items.name: Prussian Blue Tablet
items.lore: Iron hexacyanoferrate. Swallowed, it traps radioactive caesium and thallium in the gut so the body passes them instead of keeping them.

items.name: Magnetite
items.lore: Fe₃O₄, the most magnetic mineral there is. Struck by lightning it becomes lodestone; ground up it becomes ferrite.

items.name: Ferrite Magnet
items.lore: Iron oxide pressed with clay, fired, then magnetised: cheap, brittle and permanently magnetic.

items.name: Electrical Steel Lamination
items.lore: Thin sheets of silicon steel, insulated from each other, so a changing field cannot drive eddy currents through the core.

items.name: Dice Set
items.lore: Two fair dice: thirty-six outcomes, eleven totals, and seven the most likely of them.

items.name: Quantum Random Number Chip
items.lore: Single photons meet a half-silvered mirror: transmitted is 1, reflected is 0. Nothing in the universe knows the next bit in advance.

items.name: Geodetic Surveyor
items.lore: Triangulates the ground around you and lists the ores within 24 blocks, with the nearest of each.

items.name: Gauss Meter
items.lore: A Hall-effect probe: reads the magnetic field where you stand, from the planet's own to a magnet in your hand.

items.name: Geiger Counter
items.lore: Held in either hand, it clicks for every decay it hears - from what you carry and from the ground around you.

items.name: Seismic Recorder Drum
items.lore: A paper drum turned by clockwork under a hanging pen. The ground shakes, the pen does not, and the difference is written down.

items.name: Radiogenic Lead
items.lore: Lead that was once uranium, radium and radon: the stable end of a decay chain, made one nucleus at a time.

items.name: Lead Shielding Plate
items.lore: Dense, soft and cheap. Each centimetre of lead halves a gamma ray's chance of getting through.

items.name: Monazite Sand
items.lore: Heavy golden grains sorted out of beach sand: a phosphate of the rare earths, with a little thorium that keeps it faintly radioactive.

items.name: Rare Earth Oxide
items.lore: Neodymium, samarium and their cousins, so alike chemically that it took a century and a spectroscope to tell them apart.

items.name: Neodymium Alloy Blank
items.lore: Nd₂Fe₁₄B, cast and pressed, not yet magnetised. Its crystals all point the same way, waiting for a field strong enough to set them.

items.name: Samarium-Cobalt Blank
items.lore: Sm₂(Co,Fe,Cu)₁₇: harder to magnetise than neodymium, and it keeps its magnetism far hotter.

items.name: Neodymium Magnet
items.lore: The strongest permanent magnet known: a thumb-sized piece can hold a kilogram of steel. Loses its strength above about 80 °C.

items.name: Samarium-Cobalt Magnet
items.lore: A little weaker than neodymium, but it keeps its field up to 300 °C - the magnet for hot machines.

items.name: Proof Mass
items.lore: A polished cube of gold and platinum that touches nothing. Whatever path it follows is the path of free fall itself.

items.name: Time-Dilated Sample
items.lore: A crystal grown deep in a gravity well. By its own clock it took longer to form than the outside world saw.

items.name: Normal Distribution Crystal
items.lore: Faceted where the bell curve says it should be: most of it near the middle, less and less towards the edges, none past the tails.

items.name: Prior Tablet
items.lore: What you believe before you look, written down so that the evidence can change it.

items.name: Posterior Tablet
items.lore: Belief, updated by evidence. Carry one while solving a research derivation and it pays for a hint instead of Insight.

items.name: Core Drill
items.lore: A diamond-set coring bit on a hydraulic hammer. Hold it against bedrock and it cuts through - the first tool that can.

items.name: Ringwoodite
items.lore: A high-pressure form of olivine from 520 km down. Its crystals hold water: there may be more of it in the mantle than in every ocean.

items.name: Bridgmanite
items.lore: The most abundant mineral on Earth - and almost never seen, because it only exists under the pressure of the lower mantle.

items.name: Fission Fragment Mix
items.lore: Caesium, strontium, iodine and xenon: what a uranium nucleus becomes when it splits. Two billion years ago, Oklo made this on its own.

items.name: Corundum
items.lore: Aluminium oxide, as hard as anything but diamond. Coloured by a trace of iron and titanium it is sapphire; by chromium, ruby. Clear and hard, it makes the best lenses and bearings.

items.name: Garnet
items.lore: Pyrope garnet, born where crust is dragged down and squeezed. Hard, dense and cheap: the grit of every cutting wheel.

items.name: Peridot
items.lore: Gem olivine, the mineral the upper mantle is mostly made of. It forms only deep down and only reaches the surface carried up in lava.

items.name: Moissanite
items.lore: Silicon carbide, found in nature only in a few meteorites and in mantle rock. Harder than any gem but diamond, and far tougher: a drill bit of it cuts iron.

items.name: Rich Iron Chunk
items.lore: Banded iron from deep down: richer than any Overworld ore, with magnetite in its layers.

items.name: Rich Copper Chunk
items.lore: Porphyry copper, veined with gold that came up with it.

items.name: Rich Gold Chunk
items.lore: Reef gold in quartz pebbles - the kind of ore that, on Earth, carries uraninite too.

items.name: Moissanite Drill
items.lore: A moissanite-tipped drill on a netherite shank: it mines Iron-Nickel and Core Magnetite Ore, which nothing softer can.

items.name: Yellowcake
items.lore: Uranium oxide concentrate, roasted out of pitchblende: a coarse yellow-brown powder, still 99.3% uranium-238.

items.name: Fluorspar
items.lore: Calcium fluoride, which grows in veins beside calcite. The fluorine that turns uranium into a gas comes from here.

items.name: Uranium-235 Pellet
items.lore: Uranium enriched to a few percent of the fissile isotope: reactor fuel. The cascade will not go past 20%.

items.name: Uranium-238 Pellet
items.lore: Depleted uranium: what is left when the U-235 has been taken out. Dense, barely radioactive - and fertile: in a reactor it becomes plutonium.

items.name: Plutonium-239 Pellet
items.lore: Bred from uranium-238 in the reactor and taken out of its spent salt. Warm to the touch from its own alpha decay.

items.name: Graphite Moderator
items.lore: Nuclear-grade graphite. Carbon slows fission neutrons down without swallowing them, so they can split the next nucleus.

items.name: Boron Control Rod
items.lore: Boron carbide in a steel sleeve. Boron-10 drinks neutrons: push the rod in and the chain reaction slows.

items.name: Metamorphic Schist
items.lore: Basalt pressed and baked until its minerals regrew as flat, glittering mica - with the odd red garnet among them.

items.name: Light Radiation Plating
items.lore: Lead plate shaped to fit armour. Put it with any armour piece in a crafting grid: that piece then stops 10% of the radiation dose.

items.name: Medium Radiation Plating
items.lore: Lead backed with graphite, which slows the neutrons lead lets through. A plated piece stops 18% of the dose.

items.name: Heavy Radiation Plating
items.lore: Lead, graphite and boron carbide, which swallows the slowed neutrons. A plated piece stops 25% of the dose - four of them, all but 5%.

items.name: Photographic Plate
items.lore: A glass plate coated with a light-sensitive emulsion set in gelatin. Left open under the sky for an hour, it records stars far too faint for any eye.

items.name: Star Field Plate
items.lore: A developed plate of a patch of sky: thousands of stars, their positions measured to a fraction of an arcsecond.

items.name: Stellar Spectrum Plate
items.lore: Starlight spread into a spectrum on the plate. The dark lines across it give each star's temperature and what it is made of.

items.name: Deep Sky Plate
items.lore: A long exposure on a dark, moonless night: faint smudges that are whole galaxies, millions of light-years away.

items.name: Planetary Plate
items.lore: The sharpest of a thousand short exposures of a planet, taken in the instants the air held still: belts, moons, a shadow.

items.name: Hydrogen Line Map
items.lore: A chart of the 21-centimetre glow of cold hydrogen across the Galaxy. The line's Doppler shift gives how fast each cloud moves.

items.name: Pulsar Timing Record
items.lore: Arrival times of a pulsar's pulses, steady to a millionth of a second over months: a clock spun up in a dead star.

items.name: Fused Silica
items.lore: Quartz melted in the Solar Furnace and cooled to a glass. It barely expands with heat, so a mirror made of it keeps its figure.

items.name: Sapphire Window
items.lore: A disc of synthetic sapphire, aluminium oxide grown from the melt: hard, clear from ultraviolet to infrared, and it stays clear when frozen.

items.name: Heliostat Mirror
items.lore: A flat silvered mirror on a two-axis mount that turns with the Sun, so its reflection stays on one spot all day.

items.name: Cryogenic Receiver
items.lore: An amplifier cooled near absolute zero behind a sapphire window, in a copper feed. The colder it is, the less it hisses over the faint signal from the sky.

items.name: Meteoric Iron
items.lore: Iron and nickel from the core of a planetesimal that shattered billions of years ago. Etched, it shows crossed plates that grew only a degree in a million years.

items.name: Chondrite Fragment
items.lore: Stone that never melted since the planets formed: grains of olivine and metal, and among them dust older than the Sun.

items.name: Presolar Grains
items.lore: Silicon carbide stardust condensed in the winds of stars that died before the Sun was born. Moissan named the mineral moissanite when he found it in a meteorite.

items.name: Sapphire Boule
items.lore: A single crystal of aluminium oxide pulled from the melt, every atom of it in one lattice. Cut, it gives windows clear from ultraviolet to infrared.

items.name: Fluorite Boule
items.lore: Calcium fluoride grown as one crystal. It bends colours apart less than any glass, so lenses of it bring every colour to one focus.

items.name: Garnet Boule
items.lore: A synthetic garnet crystal, grown flawless. Garnets doped with rare earths are the heart of the most common solid-state lasers.

items.name: Laue Pattern
items.lore: A photographic plate exposed to X-rays scattered by a crystal: a pattern of spots that shows how its lattice planes lie. Cut along them.

items.name: Fused Silica Lens
items.lore: A lens of fused silica, ground and polished to a quarter of a wavelength. Glass has no lattice: it needs no orientation to cut.

items.name: Fluorite Lens
items.lore: A lens cut from a fluorite boule along its lattice. Paired with glass it cancels the colour error glass alone cannot.

items.name: Moissanite Lens
items.lore: Silicon carbide bends light more than diamond does: a moissanite lens is strong for its thickness, and it fires rainbows.

items.name: Schmidt Corrector Plate
items.lore: A thin, almost flat plate of fused silica, figured to a gentle aspheric curve. In front of a spherical mirror it gives a sharp image across a field many degrees wide.

items.name: Echelle Grating
items.lore: A few dozen grooves to the millimetre ruled steep in an aluminised silica blank, used at high orders: it spreads a star's light into a spectrum a hundred times finer than a prism's.

items.name: Apochromatic Objective
items.lore: Fluorite between two lenses of fused silica: three colours brought to exactly one focus, and the rest within a hair of it.

items.name: Laser Rod
items.lore: Garnet doped with neodymium, cut along its lattice and polished flat at both ends. Pumped with light, it gives back more light than it took in, all of one colour: infrared at 1064 nanometres.

items.name: Laser Head
items.lore: A laser rod between two mirrors, pumped by a flash of light, behind a Faraday isolator so no reflection can come back into it. A single frequency, steady for hours.

items.name: Faraday Isolator
items.lore: A garnet crystal in a strong magnetic field turns the plane of polarised light - the same way whichever way the light goes. Light passes out; its reflection, turned twice, cannot pass back.

items.name: Test Mass
items.lore: Forty kilograms of fused silica, polished to a few nanometres and hung on silica fibres: a mirror that does nothing but follow spacetime.

items.name: Beam Splitter
items.lore: A disc of fused silica coated so it lets exactly half the light through and reflects the other half.

items.name: Cobalt-57 Source
items.lore: Iron-54 struck by the alpha particles of radium becomes cobalt-57, which decays into iron-57 and gives off a gamma ray so sharp in energy it can be shifted by gravity across a few metres.

items.name: Black Hole Merger Record
items.lore: A chirp a fifth of a second long: two black holes of thirty suns each spiralling together a billion light-years away.

items.name: Neutron Star Merger Record
items.lore: A minute-long chirp of two neutron stars colliding. Where they merged, gold and platinum were made - and a telescope can still see it glow.

items.name: Gravitational Redshift Record
items.lore: Counts of gamma rays climbing a tower, and the source speed that brought them back into tune: gravity measured with a stopwatch of atomic nuclei.

items.name: Avogadro Record
items.lore: A thousand tracks of a clay grain in water, each one a staggering random walk, and from how far they wander: how many molecules make a mole. Perrin won the Nobel Prize for this.

items.name: Silicon Boule
items.lore: Silicon reduced from silica with carbon, then pulled from its melt as one flawless crystal: the most perfect solid people make.

items.name: Perfect Crystal Interferometer
items.lore: Three slabs cut from one silicon crystal, still joined at the base, so their lattice planes line up to a fraction of an atom: they split a neutron's wave, steer it, and bring it back together.

items.name: Gravity-Phase Record
items.lore: Neutron counts swinging between the two exits as the interferometer tilts: the fringes gravity draws on a quantum wave.

items.name: Hawking Correlation Record
items.lore: Phonon pairs straddling a sonic horizon, one on each side, correlated as Hawking said they must be: the glow of a horizon, seen.

items.name: Light Sail
items.lore: A sail of aluminised film a few microns thick, pushed by nothing but the pressure of starlight. Unfurl it high above the world, where there is no air left to drag on it, and it carries you out to the Accretion Frontier.

items.name: Interstellar Dust
items.lore: Grains of silicate and soot a tenth of a micron across, coated in ice. A hundredth of the interstellar medium by mass - and what every rocky planet was made of.

items.name: Cosmic Ray Shard
items.lore: Crystal scarred by the tracks of cosmic rays - nuclei flung across the Galaxy by supernova shocks at nearly the speed of light.

items.name: Exoplanet Core Sample
items.lore: Iron and nickel from the core of a planet that formed round another star, and was shattered in a collision long ago.

items.name: Brown Dwarf Core
items.lore: The dense heart of a failed star: too light to fuse hydrogen, heavy enough once to burn its deuterium. It still glows with the heat of its own contraction.

items.name: Cepheid Standard Candle
items.lore: The light curve of a Cepheid variable. How long it takes to pulse tells how bright it truly is (Leavitt's law) - and so how far away.

items.name: Redshift Lens
items.lore: A calibrated lens of spectra: distances from standard candles set against the redshifts of their galaxies. Every one is moving away, and the farther, the faster.

items.name: Galactic Filament
items.lore: A map of the hydrogen in a filament of gas feeding a galaxy - a thread of the cosmic web, at the scale of one galaxy.

items.name: Accretion Disk Fragment
items.lore: Slag from the inner edge of an accretion disk, frozen where it was flung out. It still remembers ten million kelvin.

items.name: Quasar Jet Filament
items.lore: A thread of the jet that a spinning black hole drives out along its axis at nearly the speed of light, wound up in magnetic field.

items.name: Planetary Nebula Shell
items.lore: The glowing shell a dying Sun-like star throws off: oxygen green, hydrogen red, round a white dwarf at its centre.

items.name: Cosmic Web Filament
items.lore: The largest structure there is: filaments of dark matter and gas a hundred million light-years long, with galaxies strung along them like dew on a web.

items.name: Transit Light Curve
items.lore: A star's brightness, dipping for a few hours as a planet crosses in front of it. The depth gives the planet's size.

items.name: Einstein Ring Lens
items.lore: A crystal from the Lensing Void that bends light round itself like a mass: a point behind it shows as a ring.

items.name: Magnetar Crust Fragment
items.lore: Iron crust from a magnetar, under a field of 10¹¹ tesla. It cracks in starquakes - and it still bends compass needles from across a room.

items.name: Tidal Shear Crystal
items.lore: A crystal pulled long and thin by a tidal force: one end fell faster than the other.

items.name: Hawking Quanta
items.lore: The last light of a tiny black hole, caught as it evaporated. Hotter the smaller the hole was.

items.name: Black Swan Feather
items.lore: Proof that the improbable happens. For centuries every swan was white - until one was not.

items.name: Chirp Signal Record
items.lore: The rising whoop of two compact stars spiralling together: their gravitational waves climb in pitch and strength until they merge.

items.name: Merger Remnant
items.lore: What is left when two compact stars become one: a single spinning hole, ringing down to stillness.

items.name: Entropy Die
items.lore: A die worn perfectly fair. Every face is equally likely - which is to say it carries the most entropy a die can: log₂ 6 bits a throw.

items.name: Litz Wire
items.lore: Hundreds of thin copper strands, each insulated and woven so every one takes its turn at the outside: at high frequency current crowds to a wire's skin, and this gives it more skin.

items.name: Mu-Metal Shield
items.lore: Four parts nickel to one of iron, annealed in hydrogen: so permeable that a magnetic field would rather run through it than past what it shields. Carried in the off hand, it keeps you from being Magnetized.

items.name: Faraday Cage Mesh
items.lore: A fine copper mesh. Charges in it rearrange until the field inside is zero. Carried in the off hand, it shields you from Decoherence.

items.name: Waveguide
items.lore: A rectangular copper pipe that carries microwaves the way a pipe carries water - no wave longer than twice its width gets through.

items.name: Bitter Plate
items.lore: A copper disc cut with a slit and pierced with cooling holes. Stacked into a helix, Bitter plates make the strongest steady magnets there are.

items.name: Rail Armature
items.lore: A copper slug that bridges a railgun's two rails: the current through it and the field of the rails push it out at kilometres a second.

items.name: Lonsdaleite
items.lore: Hexagonal diamond, made only in the shock of an impact - harder, in places, than diamond itself.

items.name: Hall Bar Chip
items.lore: A strip of two-dimensional electrons at a kelvin and ten tesla. Its Hall resistance sits on plateaus at exactly h/(νe²): a resistance standard set by nature.

items.name: Plasma Thruster Nozzle
items.lore: A magnetic nozzle of lonsdaleite and iron: plasma pushed out along its field lines leaves faster than any chemical exhaust.

items.name: Lithium Ingot
items.lore: The lightest metal, won from brine. Soft enough to cut with a knife; it floats on oil and burns crimson.

items.name: Lithium-6 Ingot
items.lore: Lithium enriched in its lighter isotope. One neutron splits it into helium and tritium - which is how a fusion blanket breeds its fuel.

items.name: Thorium-232 Pellet
items.lore: Three times as common as uranium, and not fissile itself - but a neutron makes it uranium-233, which is.

items.name: Polonium-210 Source
items.lore: A speck of polonium giving off so many alpha particles that it is warm to the touch. Harmless at arm's length; deadly inside you.

items.name: Technetium-99m Vial
items.lore: An excited nucleus that gives off one clean gamma ray and calms down within hours: the most used medical isotope in the world.

items.name: Californium-252 Neutron Source
items.lore: A microgram of californium splits by itself often enough to give off two million neutrons a second.

items.name: Spent Fuel Rod
items.lore: A fuel rod after three years in a reactor: still mostly uranium, but laced with fission products a million times more radioactive.

items.name: Nuclear Waste Glass
items.lore: Fission products melted into borosilicate glass: it will hold them for the hundred thousand years they need.

items.name: Fusion Blanket Tile
items.lore: Lithium-6 behind lead and graphite. It catches the fusion neutrons, turns their energy into heat, and breeds tritium as it does.

items.name: Hafnium-178m2 Isomer
items.lore: A nucleus that holds 2.4 MeV in a high-spin state for thirty-one years: a gram of it stores as much as a tonne of TNT.

items.name: Hafnium Dust
items.lore: What is left when an isomer gives up its energy: ordinary hafnium.

items.name: Kilonova Ash
items.lore: Gold, platinum and lanthanides made in a second by the rapid neutron capture of a neutron-star merger, and thrown out at a fifth of the speed of light.

items.name: Burst Afterglow Crystal
items.lore: The fading afterglow of a gamma-ray burst - the brightest explosions there are, seen across the Universe.

items.name: Aquifer Sample
items.lore: Water from a confined aquifer, tens of thousands of years old: rain from the last ice age, still on its way.

items.name: Ice Core
items.lore: A cylinder of ice drilled from a glacier. Every layer is a year of snow, and its trapped bubbles are samples of the air of that year.

items.name: Permafrost Sample
items.lore: Soil frozen for thousands of years, holding the carbon of the plants that grew before it froze.

items.name: Survey Satellite
items.lore: A telescope pointed down instead of up, with solar wings and a radio. Flown high enough, it photographs the ground.

items.name: Satellite Image Plate
items.lore: The ground seen from orbit, in visible and infrared: rivers, faults, and the heat of what lies under the surface.

items.name: Lithospheric Plate Fragment
items.lore: Rock from the base of a tectonic plate, where the cold, rigid lithosphere rides on the soft mantle below.

items.name: Planetary Core Sample
items.lore: Iron and nickel from two planets' cores, pressed together to the pressure at a core's centre: the stuff every rocky planet sinks to its middle.

items.name: Strain Sensor
items.lore: A fused-silica fibre that changes its light when it stretches by a part in a billion.

items.name: Precision Gyroscope
items.lore: A fused-quartz sphere, the roundest object ever made, spinning in a vacuum. Space itself turns its axis. Carried in the off hand, it holds you steady against Frame Drag and Tidal Strain.

items.name: Geodesic Compass
items.lore: A compass that points along the straightest path through curved spacetime - which is the path a falling body takes.

items.name: Lense-Thirring Vortex Core
items.lore: A knot of spacetime twisted round by a spinning mass: anything near it is dragged round with it.

items.name: Gravitational Wave Echo
items.lore: Faint repeats after a merger's ringdown - if a horizon is not quite a horizon, the waves bounce. Play it in the Accretion Frontier and something answers.

items.name: Negative Energy Lattice
items.lore: Casimir cavities stacked by the million: in each, the vacuum between the plates holds less energy than the vacuum outside.

items.name: Warp Bubble Core
items.lore: A bubble of flat space ready to be pushed through curved space. Used, it anchors where you stand; the anchored bubble brings you back there once.

items.name: Anchored Warp Bubble
items.lore: A warp bubble tied to the place it was anchored. Used, it carries you back there and is spent.

items.name: Unruh Thermometer
items.lore: A detector that clicks when it is accelerated through empty space: to it, the vacuum is a warm bath, T = ħa/2πck.

items.name: Firewall Shard
items.lore: If information escapes a black hole, the entanglement across its horizon must break - and a broken horizon would burn whatever falls in. A shard of that hypothetical wall of fire.

items.name: Soft Hair Filament
items.lore: Zero-energy excitations on a horizon that remember what fell in: a black hole may not be quite as bald as it seems.

items.name: Planck Area Tile
items.lore: The smallest area there is, in loop quantum gravity: 8πγℓₚ²√(j(j+1)), where a spin network's link pierces a surface.

items.name: Spin Network Node
items.lore: A node of a spin network: a grain of volume, its faces the links that join it to its neighbours. Space is built from these.

items.name: Causal Set Seed
items.lore: Events scattered at random into spacetime, with nothing but which came before which. From that order alone, geometry grows.

items.name: ER Bridge Thread
items.lore: Two entangled particles, and a wormhole too small to pass through joining them: Einstein-Rosen equals Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen.

items.name: Fixed-Point Lattice
items.lore: Gravity's strength, run to ever shorter distances, settles on a fixed value instead of blowing up: a theory safe all the way down.

items.name: Page Curve Record
items.lore: The entropy of a black hole's radiation: rising as it evaporates, until halfway - then falling back to zero. Information comes out. Carried in the off hand, it puts your hotbar back in order (no Information Loss).

items.name: Island Fragment
items.lore: A region inside the horizon that belongs, after the Page time, to the radiation outside: the island that makes the curve turn over.

items.name: Holographic Screen
items.lore: A surface that holds everything in the volume behind it, one bit per four Planck areas.

items.name: Boundary CFT Chip
items.lore: A quantum field theory without gravity, on a boundary - which is the same theory as gravity in the space inside it.

items.name: Poisson Clock
items.lore: A clock that ticks at random: each tick a decay in its radium, the waits between them falling off exponentially. It keeps perfect average time and never says when.

items.name: Markov Chain Link
items.lore: A link that remembers only the one before it. Chain enough of them and the past stops mattering at all.

items.name: Confidence Interval Gauge
items.lore: A gauge that shows not a value but a range, and how sure it is. Carried in the off hand, it steadies the luck of what you drink (no Variance).

items.name: Monte Carlo Sample Pack
items.lore: A billion random points, drawn and sorted: the answer to an integral too hard to do any other way, to a part in thirty thousand.

items.name: Partition Function Matrix
items.lore: Z = Σ e^(−E/kT), summed over every state a system can be in. Everything else - energy, entropy, pressure - is a derivative of it.

items.name: Large Deviation Shard
items.lore: A record of something that was not supposed to happen - and the exponentially small odds it beat.

items.name: Ergodic Mixer Core
items.lore: A mixer that visits every state there is, given time - so its average over time is its average over all of them.

items.name: Protostellar Ember
items.lore: A shard of a star not yet lit, still glowing with the heat of its own collapse. A furnace of a fuel: it burns for a long time.

blocks.name: Antisoil
blocks.lore: Soil of the Antiverse, made of antiprotons, antineutrons and positrons. It is stable only because everything around it is antimatter too; brought into contact with ordinary matter, a gram of it would release about 180 TJ.

blocks.name: Ex Nihilo Engine
blocks.lore: Creation from nothing, made a machine. It does not convert energy - it simply has it: it gives unlimited FE to every block beside it, and charges the items of every player within 16 blocks.

blocks.name: Magnetite Bricks
blocks.lore: Bricks of magnetite (Fe3O4), the most magnetic mineral in nature. Iron oxide is dense, so it also shields: it stops gamma rays about two thirds as well as lead, and neutrons three times better.

blocks.name: Lead Bricks
blocks.lore: Bricks of lead shielding. Lead is dense and has many electrons, so it stops gamma rays well - about half of them every 1.3 cm - but it does little against neutrons. Shields as well as the Lead Shielding Block.

blocks.name: Lead Hazard Panel
blocks.lore: Lead shielding striped yellow and black to mark a radiation area. It shields as well as the Lead Shielding Block.

blocks.name: Oklo Rock
blocks.lore: Host rock of the Natural Reactor, modelled on Oklo in Gabon, where two billion years ago groundwater slowed neutrons enough for uranium ore to run as a fission reactor for hundreds of thousands of years. It is still slightly radioactive.

blocks.name: Mantle Breach
blocks.lore: A hole bored through bedrock by the Core Drill. Step into it and you fall to the Planetary Interior; on arrival a second breach opens in the floor beside you, and stepping into that one brings you back up. It cannot be broken or moved.

blocks.name: Inner Core Boundary
blocks.lore: The floor of the Planetary Interior: the edge of the solid inner core, 5,150 km down. Iron here is crystallised under 330 GPa and about 5,400 C - as hot as the Sun's surface, yet solid because the pressure will not let it melt. No tool breaks it.

blocks.name: Impact Breccia
blocks.lore: Rock shattered and welded back together in the instant of an impact. It lines a meteorite crater's bowl and rim.

blocks.name: Iron Meteorite
blocks.lore: The iron-nickel mass of a meteorite, half buried where it struck. Found in craters out in open country.

blocks.name: Chondrite
blocks.lore: A stony meteorite: rock that has not melted since the planets formed. Found in craters out in open country.
